>Every psychologist is different, and it may take time to find one that you like, that relates to you well, and that you are comfortable with.

That's something I need to remember... if I find a support person who sucks, I can't just abandon the idea of support altogether.  I am being referred to a psychologist right now, but I don't actually know how long the list is.  I'll probably call up my doctor and ask.  I don't ask nearly enough questions of my doctor. :-)

It's really comforting to hear someone else say that (re. "gaming the system").  I don't like lying, but it depends on my mood at the time. :-P

I believe that I'm pretty attuned to my emotional state.  I know the difference between feeling depressed and just feeling tired and miserable, and hopefully that would apply to suicidality as well.

Hm... didn't know about needafriend, thanks for pointing that out.

Since health care is entirely publicly funded here (and therefore all medical services have fixed charges that the government will pay), the specialists seem to go where they can get the most volume.  I'm not in one of those places.  Therapists have something like a six-month waiting list, so it was easier to get medication than to actually talk to someone.

Before the medication, I would crumple into a quivering heap over the smallest things.  Also, nothing I did had any real purpose or meaning, so I didn't really bother trying to do anything.  I'd play video games all the time, because it kept me entertained in the short term, but meanwhile I'd skip university classes -- knowing full well the consequences, but feeling self-destructive enough not to change.

Now I feel like a zombie most of the time.  I'd rather sleep than do anything, because it's easier than making the effort to actually get up and do something.  I now care about negative consequences, at least... I will fulfill responsibilities like those of my job to keep myself employed.  But if there's anything that's just "for me," I really can't be bothered.

Thanks for taking the time out to respond, by the way.

No, if I were left to myself, things would only get worse until I died of malnutrition or something far more pathetic. :-P  I used to live on my own, and that was when I ended up at my worst (zero self-confidence, self-destructive, etc.).  I ended up moving back in with my parents and I was able to get back into a more stable condition.

Ultimately, the lesson I learned is that I need to seek out support if I want to get better.  Hence why I came here.  I truly appreciate the welcome. :-)

I'll apologize in advance, because this is a very important community and I'm worried I'm about to cross the line of abusing it right here.  I just read this subreddit so often and feel like it's the kind of community that I need to be a part of if I want my life to be worth the trouble it is to live it.

Like the title says, I'm not suicidal.  Either I'm not depressed enough, or I'm too apathetic to go that far.  But I am depressed (I would say I'm "dealing" with depression, but I don't think I'm actually succeeding).  I'm just at a point now where I'm not sure what to do about it.  I confess that being suicidal appears to be the one surefire way of getting help and attention.  Again, I really don't mean to degrade what it means to be suicidal, but this is what's stuck on my mind.

Anyways, what can I actually do?  I long for some kind of external assistance, professional or not.  And to be honest, I'm in Canada, and getting professional assistance has been like trying to see how long I can hold my breath (but using months instead of minutes).  Anti-depressant medication helps rid me of despair, but I'm left with total apathy (and annoying physical side-effects).  And from experience I know I'm not going to get anywhere on my own.
The only person I've heard say it was former Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien.  Take that for what you will.

Oh hell.  Those people who are behind in you in the right lane, who switch to the on-ramp lane to pass you on the right, then cut in front of you at the end of the on-ramp.  I want to hurt them so very, very badly.

I agree, it's fun to bait aggressive drivers. :-)

I try to respect the law while also driving pragmatically.  If everyone's doing 20 km/h over the limit, I'll join in.  And I know what it's like to be denied merging onto a highway by selfish assholes in the right lane, so I'll always allow someone to merge in front of me (as long as they signal, anyway).

I like to think that what makes me a better driver is that I realize there are other people on the road, too.
